items.objection: The rename rebuilds five endpoints, the instance create/filter and their handlers under new names. If one renamed endpoint or handler loses the old access check (for example it is registered outside the module's 'resources' policy group, or the group check on the new resourceSchemaId filter is dropped), a group member or a user from another group can read, change or delete another group's schemas, or list another group's instances by passing a foreign resourceSchemaId. Every acceptance criterion still passes, because AC-1, AC-3, AC-4 and AC-5 are all written for the group owner only, and blast_radius says touches_authz: false. Today's rules are not visible in the generated files (F-4), so nothing records what 'same access rules' means.
items.evidence: F-4: 'Resources endpoints (/resources/types*, /resources/instances*) show no role or group restriction ... Whether owner-only or member-only rules are enforced inside those operations is not visible'; AC-1 role: owner only, 'same access rules'; blast_radius touches_authz: false
items.alternative: Add an acceptance criterion: before the rename, record how each /resources/types operation and each instance create/list-with-filter call responds to (a) a group member who is not the owner, (b) a signed-in user from another group and (c) a filter that names another group's schema. After the rename, /resources/schemas and resourceSchemaId must give exactly the same responses in all three cases, and every renamed endpoint must stay under the Resources module's 'resources' policy.

items.objection: AC-9 only requires that the application starts and allows existing schemas and instances to be removed, but it sets no limit on what the removal may touch. A migration that drops and recreates tables runs on every database the application starts against. Nothing in the story prevents that migration from also removing property definitions or values linked to other data, rows in other modules that point to resources, or data in a database that is not a developer's own (a shared or demo database). Such a loss is irreversible, and the Down step would only bring back empty tables.
items.evidence: AC-9: 'existing resource schemas and instances may be removed in the process (owner decision: development data only)'; why: 'no real data yet'
items.alternative: Extend AC-9 so that only Resources module tables (schemas, their property definitions, instances, their property values) may be emptied, and rows of ManagementGroups and Users (groups, members, users) are the same before and after the new version starts. Add an out-of-scope line recording that the owner confirmed no shared or demo database holds Resources data at merge time.

items.objection: The 016 migration is generated on top of the unmerged 015 branch. If 015 is rebased or its migration is regenerated before or while it merges to main (which D-4a permits), the 016 migration and model snapshot no longer match the history on main. A developer's database that already has either version applied then fails to start, or startup reports pending model changes. AC-9 was tested only against the pre-rebase history, so no check catches this.
items.evidence: Proposal notes: 'Base branch is 015-resource-time-buffer, which is not merged to main (28 commits ahead); expect a rebase when 015 changes.'; AC-9
items.alternative: Add an ordering guard: 016 merges only after 015 is on main. After the final rebase, the 016 migration is regenerated, AC-9 is re-run against a database created from main, and a check that the model has no pending changes passes.

items.objection: AC-2 makes the old addresses return 404, but the old field names fail silently. A stale frontend (a cached bundle, an open tab, a developer's unrebuilt client) calling GET /resources/instances?resourceTypeId=X gets the unfiltered list of all the group's instances instead of an error. POST /resources/instances with resourceTypeId arrives with an empty resourceSchemaId. The owner sees wrong lists with no visible failure.
items.evidence: AC-2 covers only 'an old /resources/types address'; AC-3/AC-5 introduce resourceSchemaId; F-1: resourceTypeId is a body field and a query parameter today
items.alternative: Add an acceptance criterion: a request that still sends resourceTypeId (body or query) is rejected with a validation error naming resourceSchemaId. Alternatively, add an explicit out-of-scope line accepting that old field names are silently ignored, and require that backend and frontend are always started together.

items.objection: The owner rejected keeping database names because 'the old name would stay in the database forever'. Yet no acceptance criterion checks the database, only the API description (AC-6) and messages (AC-7). A rename that moves tables and columns but keeps old primary key, foreign key, index or sequence names (such as ...ResourceTypeId) passes every AC and leaves exactly the leftover the owner wanted removed.
items.evidence: rejected_alternatives: 'Owner chose the full rename: no real data exists, the old name would stay in the database forever'; AC-6 scope limited to 'the generated API description'
items.alternative: Add an acceptance criterion: after the migration, no table, column, constraint, index or sequence name in the Resources database area contains 'resource_type' or 'ResourceType' (excluding PropertyDataType/dataType).
